page.layout: One page of text in verse, with stanzas set in italic. Headings are centred above each poem. Right margin: two small quotation-like marks beside the fifth poem. Right margin also shows bleed-through from the other side (ignored). Catchword at lower right, signature at foot left of centre.

main_text.head: IIII. Wigandus Heimelius Grentzenbachensis.

p.i: HEimelio do laureain, Heimelio do gemmulam.

main_text.p: Lusu, jocis & otio Non crescit eruditio. Labore Divi munera Mortalibus vendunt sua.
main_text.head: V. Simon Lucanus Neocuriensis.

p.i: UT decus est horto laurus, laurusq; corona, Pulcra corona coma, coma Nympha, Nympha chorea:
Sic virtus arti decus est, artiq; juventa, Docta juventa Schola, schola templis, templa colonis. Hac tua te moneat laetissima laurea Simon.

main_text.head: VI. Philippus Halgans Grunbergensis.

p.i: SAúlne inter vates? inter ferus anser olores? Non ita: doctrina est factus & arte ciéur. Ergò vola huc, &, ut orneris pulcrè, caput unum Da mihi: Praposito catera dono coco. Ad vigila libris: damnosa est alea pernox: In serto gemma est (ut placet?) ista tuo.

main_text.head: VII. Theodorus de Ana Geismariensis.
main_text.p: QUi Theodore colis praesignia dona Dei, artes, Immemor haud unquam nominis ipse tui, Te manet haec merces, proprio tibi adepta labore: Cuiq; sua est virtus, non aliena, decus.
main_text.head: VIII. Michaël Lambertus Geismariensis.

p.i: AT tibi nunc textam tribuo Lamberte corollam, Qua damnosi expers senii, tua tempora circum Floreat, aeternoq; nitens scintillet honore, Donec ad aequoreis ignotos fluctibus ignes Clara Ariadnea rutilabunt signa corona.

page.notes: Page number read as "13"; the first glyph is uncertain. Right-margin marks beside the fifth poem are small quotation-like signs, transcribed as notes. Faint "A5" at lower left is not clearly printed text and was omitted. Bleed-through from the facing page was ignored. Uncertain readings: "laureain" (possibly lauream), "Aúlne" (accent over u uncertain), "ciéur", "Praposito". The section initials H, U, S, Q and A are large woodcut letters, joined to their first words.
